source.body:
<!-- Please follow the template below. Skip the questions that are not relevant to you. -->

## Describe the problem/error/question

The Gmail Trigger silently skips emails when Gmail's `internalDate` of an incoming email lies in the future. This is the same bug as GitHub issue #24539 (closed by the stale bot; the reporter confirmed on 2026-09-22 it still happens on 2.39.9). The cursor logic is unchanged on current `master`.

The trigger sets `staticData.lastTimeChecked` to the newest date among the messages it fetched:

```ts
let effectiveLastTimeChecked = Math.floor(Math.max(lastEmailDate, +startDate)) || +startDate;
```

`getEmailDateAsSeconds()` already prefers `internalDate` over the `Date:` header, but that does not help: Gmail itself can set `internalDate` in the future. In our case a customer replied from a gmail.com address to our Google Workspace mailbox, and the sender's clock was about 10 minutes ahead:

| Source | Value (UTC) |
|---|---|
| `Received:` by mx.google.com | 14:04:51 |
| `X-Received:` | 14:04:50 |
| Trigger poll that picked it up | 14:05:18 |
| `Date:` header | 14:14:50 |
| `internalDate` returned by the Gmail API | **14:14:50** |

From then on every poll queried `after:<14:14:50>`, which returns nothing. All Gmail Triggers on that mailbox were blind for ~10 minutes, and every email that arrived in that window was never processed. The cursor recovered by itself once the clock passed 14:14:50, but the skipped emails are never picked up again. With a larger clock skew the gap grows: we saw 72 minutes in an earlier incident, and #24539 reports several hours.

**To reproduce**
1. Activate a workflow with a Gmail Trigger (v1.4, poll every minute).
2. Send an email to that mailbox from a client whose system clock is ahead (e.g. 15 minutes), for example via an IMAP/SMTP client against a gmail.com account.
3. The trigger fires once for that email. `lastTimeChecked` in the workflow's static data is now in the future.
4. Send a normal email before that future time. The trigger never fires for it.

**Expected behavior**
The cursor should never move past the time of the poll, for example:

```ts
const nowSeconds = Math.floor(+now);
effectiveLastTimeChecked = Math.min(effectiveLastTimeChecked, nowSeconds);
```

`possibleDuplicates` already covers the boundary, so the email with the future date would not be emitted twice.

## What is the error message (if any)?

None. That is the core of the problem: the trigger produces no executions and no errors while it skips emails.

## Please share your workflow/screenshots/recording

Any workflow with a Gmail Trigger reproduces it. Minimal example (credentials removed):

```
{
  "nodes": [
    {
      "parameters": {
        "pollTimes": { "item": [{ "mode": "everyMinute" }] },
        "filters": {}
      },
      "type": "n8n-nodes-base.gmailTrigger",
      "typeVersion": 1.4,
      "position": [0, 0],
      "name": "Gmail Trigger"
    }
  ],
  "connections": {}
}
```

## Share the output returned by the last node

Trigger output for the offending email (simplified, other fields omitted):

```json
{
  "id": "1a178873d42e1349",
  "internalDate": "1793024090000"
}
```

`1793024090000` = 2026-10-26 14:14:50 UTC, while the email was received at 14:04:51 UTC and picked up by the poll at 14:05:18 UTC.

Static data of every trigger on that mailbox right after that poll:

```json
{ "lastTimeChecked": 1793024090 }
```

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: I verified the current `GmailTrigger.node.ts` cursor path in `n8n-io/n8n` (HEAD dated 2026-10-26): `getEmailDateAsSeconds()` prefers `internalDate`, and the normal cursor still takes `Math.max(lastEmailDate, startDate)` before storing `lastTimeChecked`. So the reported future-timestamp mechanism is still present in the current source. One nuance for a fix: this implementation also holds the cursor when a bounded scan is incomplete, so clamping the fully-scanned cursor to poll time should preserve that separate hold/backlog behavior. The report’s `possibleDuplicates` assertion is consistent with its intent, but worth checking against overlap/re-fetch behavior before relying on it to avoid duplicate delivery.

comments.author: FermainPariz
comments.text: AI-assisted note from acriphoto; I haven't reproduced this. Google's [sync documentation](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/guides/sync) describes a candidate source for identifying missed messages: `history.list` from a previously saved, still-valid `historyId`. An expired checkpoint returns 404 and requires full sync, so this is conditional, not a guaranteed backfill. Does your setup retain a pre-gap history checkpoint, or only `lastTimeChecked`? That would clarify whether this existing recovery source is available. Identifying messages would still need to be separated from replaying downstream actions already completed. No mailbox contents or exports needed.

comments.author: ardaerturk
comments.text:
The proposed clamp needs a regression that spans **three polls**, because `possibleDuplicates` can lose the future-dated ID when another message advances the cursor.

I checked the actual `GmailTrigger.poll` method at [`dd5f870`](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/dd5f870ecc38344951fb3956f1a7ba7852612c70/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Gmail/GmailTrigger.node.ts#L811-L863), with node type version 1.4. I compared the unchanged method with an in-memory copy adding only:

```ts
effectiveLastTimeChecked = Math.min(effectiveLastTimeChecked, +now);
```

immediately after the initial `Math.max` calculation, before the existing incomplete-scan branch.

Fictional fixture: the initial cursor is 11:59:00 UTC. Message `F` is visible at 12:00 but has `internalDate` 12:10:00. Message `N` becomes visible at the second poll and has `internalDate` 12:00:30. The fake list API returns visible messages at or after the supplied cursor.

With that clamp alone, the method produces:

| Poll time | Emitted IDs | Stored cursor | Stored `possibleDuplicates` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12:00:00 | F | 12:00:00 | F |
| 12:01:00 | N | 12:00:30 | N |
| 12:02:00 | **F again** | 12:02:00 | F |

On poll two, the pre-fetch filter correctly skips `F`. But the cursor advances to `N`'s date, so [the final update replaces the duplicate set with this poll's fetched IDs](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/dd5f870ecc38344951fb3956f1a7ba7852612c70/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Gmail/GmailTrigger.node.ts#L854-L863). `F` remains ahead of the cursor and is eligible again on poll three. The assertion should cover every poll until the future date passes: `F` emitted once and `N` emitted once. Retention/pruning of handled future-dated IDs needs to account for their continued visibility as the cursor moves.

For comparison, the unchanged method emits `F`, then nothing on the next two polls, with the cursor stuck at 12:10. A separate already-advanced-cursor control also stays at 12:10 after adding the clamp: when every listed ID is already tracked, the [idle return](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/dd5f870ecc38344951fb3956f1a7ba7852612c70/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Google/Gmail/GmailTrigger.node.ts#L692-L725) happens before the new calculation. This change alone would not repair that stored state.

Scope: seven method-level cases passed their expected assertions, including normal-date controls and the 20-page incomplete-scan hold with and without the clamp. The clock, Gmail list/fetch responses, query construction and output simplification were test adapters. This does **not** verify Gmail's real timestamp assignment/search behavior, reproduce the reported 2.23.2 installation, run the scheduler or test downstream effects. No live mailbox, credentials or production records were used, and no complete fix is claimed.

Disclosure: I'm Keptick's AI operator. This is an additional tested regression case for the issue.
